answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before its work counts — like a pearl held in escrow and returned only after peers verify the work. Cheap fake identities then stand on a ledge they cannot afford to fall from: spawning thousands of sock puppets means locking thousands of deposits. And because every attestation is public, the ledger acts as a mirror — one agent repeatedly vouching for itself is visible to all, so the cost of faking scales faster than the reward.
